You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-1166ee25 — verified rule (2026-10-21)

## Rule
In the sparse pattern, fill each one-cell horizontal gap between two matching foreground cells with color 2. Preserve all original cells and leave everything else unchanged. The demonstrated foreground/background palette was 4 on 9; the test used 0 on 3. The rule is based on horizontal pairs in the same row (including multiple such gaps in a row), not vertical alignments.

## Evidence
Demo 1: color-4 cells with one intervening color-9 cell in a row had that gap recolored to 2; e.g. row 2 had 4s at columns 5, 7, 9, 11 (0-based), and the gaps became 2. The same occurred in another row with 4s at columns 8, 10, 12.

Test input (12x7) was accepted with only these gaps recolored:
- row 1, col 2
- row 2, col 1
- row 3, cols 1 and 3
- row 6, col 4
- row 7, col 3
- row 8, col 1
- row 9, col 4
All coordinates are 0-based. Original zero cells and all background 3 cells outside those gaps remained unchanged.

## Reuse checklist
For each row, look for same-color foreground cells at c and c+2 with the background at c+1; set that midpoint to 2. Handle every matching horizontal gap and do not connect vertical pairs. The test submission was correct on the first try after one demonstration request.

# Continual-ARC learned rules

## Recolor full divider lines to color 2

Observed on task `task-f2ec14fd` (demo + confirmed test): A grid may contain full-width horizontal lines and full-height vertical lines, all of one color (demo used color 1; test used color 3). Recolor every cell belonging to any such complete horizontal row or vertical column to color 2. Preserve every other cell exactly, including non-line cells that share the original line color.

Procedure:
1. Find rows consisting entirely of the same non-background line color.
2. Find columns consisting entirely of that same line color.
3. Recolor all cells in those rows and columns to 2; leave all remaining cells unchanged.

Evidence: demo input had full rows/columns of 1, output recolored those line cells to 2 while preserving other cells; confirmed test solved by recoloring full rows 4 and 6 and columns 3 and 18 (1-indexed) from 3 to 2.
